text:
dylan_cust: Hey, noticed our webhook consumers started getting invalid JSON from structured_output after last night's model flip. Some arrays are null now, parser fails on client side.

maria: sorry about that — can you paste a failing response and the request ID? we can triage.

dylan_cust: sample response (truncated for privacy):
```json
{"order_id": "1234", "items": null, "total": 42.50}
```
Our schema expects items: [ {id, qty} ] not null. request_id=rc-3f9b2a

maria: thanks. did you switch model pinning recently or did this start right after our 04:00 UTC deploy?

dylan_cust: it correlates with your 04:07 deploy — we started seeing failures at 04:10. No change on our side.

maria: assigning into eng. @alex can you take a look?

alex: on it. first pass — is this happening for streaming responses or non-streaming? streaming chunk boundaries can produce truncated json if chunking changed.

dylan_cust: non-streaming for this endpoint (we use /v1/generate with structured_output=true). payload below: 
```json
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood/llama-4b:2026-03-16", "structured_output": true, "prompt": "serialize order...", "max_tokens": 300 }
```

maria: deploy-bot logs show model tag rotated to redwood/llama-4b:2026-03-17-canary at 04:05.

deploy-bot: rc logs attached for rc-3f9b2a: route=support-prod generate request, latency=120ms, model=llama-4b:2026-03-17-canary, worker=gw-03.

alex: ok repro attempt: calling generate with that model and same prompt. getting consistent output but with items key occasionally set to null when the model emits the phrase "no items" — downstream serializer is turning an empty list into null. suspect model tokenization/serialization policy changed for empty collections.

anya: tagging product — we changed structured_output postprocessing recently to normalize empty containers, but that landed on canary yesterday. could be a normalization tweak that maps [] -> null in some edge cases.

maria: customer impact: multiple ACME webhook retries failing JSON parse, causing billing alerts. they classify as P1.

sre_oncall: suggest temporary mitigation: rollback canary to previous model or add a middleware that coerces null -> [] for the items field for that tenant. which is faster?

alex: fastest is a model pin on their account to previous model (llama-4b:2026-03-16). we can also hotfix postprocessor to preserve array type but that needs careful tests.

maria: asked dylan if pin is acceptable. dylan_cust: yes, pin to 2026-03-16 until fix.

alex: created internal issue INF-4729 with repro steps, sample prompt, and unit test that asserts items is always an array. root cause likely a change in the model-side structured serializer handling of empty sequences -> emitted null token sequence.

anya: adding product acceptance criteria: structured_output must preserve collection types (array vs null) per schema. no implicit nullification.

maria: next steps: 1) pin dylan_cust org to prior model (maria). 2) eng: urgent patch to postproc to coerce null->[] only for backward compatibility, landed behind feature flag (alex). 3) product to schedule revert or formal normalization change (anya). 4) SRE to monitor for other tenants affected (sre_oncall).

alex: working on patch now, will open canary PR and try to push a hotfix to prod canary channel in ~30m. logging added to detect null array occurrences and tenant ids.

dylan_cust: thanks all — ping me when pin is active. our engineers will resume after that.

maria: pin applied to org acme-ops, confirmed. please validate.

dylan_cust: validated, webhook consumers green. thanks for fast turnaround :trophy:

maria: closing loop: follow-up postmortem will include exact serialization diff and whether we should tighten model onboarding checks for structured_output changes. assigning INF-4729 -> eng oncall for next 48h.
